summary: Tested the 'Timer Chiamata' feature with two peer pages (viewer and sender) in one chromium using fake media (375x667). Stats: PASS. The timer and stats are hidden before the call and while it rings. After Rispondi, viewer-call-stats and sender-call-stats (plus sender-call-pill over the preview) appear at 00:00 and count up every second (00:00 -> 00:11 observed). Quality goes from 'Misuro…' to 'Buona' within about 3-4s on both pages. Metrics showed real values: viewer 'Ricevo' 1.1-1.2 Mbit/s, 19-20 fps, 0-1 ms, 0%, 'Video 3840 × 1920'; sender 'Invio' 1.1 Mbit/s, 19-20 fps, 1-2 ms, 0%. In viewer fullscreen, viewer-call-pill is centred in the top bar (135,20, 105x32) and counts up (00:03 -> 00:06). Hangup from fullscreen, from viewer-hangup-button and from sender-hangup-button removes the card and pill on both pages. A second call restarts at 00:00 'Misuro…' and reaches 'Buona' after 4s. Cancel regression: PASS. Decline regression: INTERMITTENT FAIL, see rca_of_issue. Two minor UX issues: the quality label flickers between Buona and Media, and the viewer stays in fullscreen after the call ends.

ui_bugs.issue: Tapping Rifiuta right after the incoming card appears on a 2nd or later call (peerS already open) does not notify the sender. The sender stays on 'Squilla: attendi che risponda dal visore.' until the 45s timeout. Reproduced in 2 of 2 immediate declines on calls after the first: cases B and E, plus the earlier run. Declining after 1.5s works (cases C and D), and an immediate decline on the very first call works (case A).

After hangup (from either side) in fullscreen, the viewer stays in fullscreen on a black stage with 'In attesa del video…' and only the exit button showing. viewer-status and viewer-incoming are hidden there, so a new incoming call (Rispondi/Rifiuta) cannot be seen until the user exits fullscreen by hand.

issues: The quality label flickers between Buona and Media every 2s when the stream sits at about 20fps: quality() needs fps >= 20 for Buona and the fake camera alternates 19/20. Seen on the sender (t=6s Media, then Buona) and on the viewer (Media at 19 fps). Use smoothing (for example an average of the last 3 samples or hysteresis) or a lower fps threshold such as 18.
Viewer at 375x667: the stats card sits below the hangup button at y=533 and is only partly visible until the controls ScrollView is scrolled. Acceptable, but users may not notice it.

action_items: HIGH: Fix the decline race in backend/stage.html handlers.decline. If canali[attesa.peer] is missing or not yet open, queue the decline: keep the dc reference and on dc 'open' send {t:'decline'}, then close it. Alternatively, on the sender, treat the viewer closing the data channel or the media call before 'connected' as a decline. Today the PeerJS MediaConnection.close() on an unanswered call never reaches the caller.
MEDIUM: In the 'ended' handler in viewer.tsx, call setFull(false) so fullscreen exits after hangup and the user can see incoming calls. Or show viewer-incoming inside fullscreen.
LOW: Stop the quality label flickering (smoothing/hysteresis or fps threshold of about 18).

LOW: In annullata(peer) in stage.html, also check that the closing dc is the current canali[peer]. A late close of the previous call's data channel (closed 300ms after fineS) shares the same sender peer id and could cancel a newer incoming call from the same sender.
critical_code_review_comments: stage.html avviaStats: an in-flight async getStats() can resolve after fermaStats() and still post a stale {type:'stats'} after 'ended'. Guard it with a local token (const id = timerStats; ... if (timerStats !== id) return). In practice the 2nd call started correctly with 'Misuro…'.

viewer.tsx/sender.tsx: startedAt uses (t ?? Date.now()) and is only reset on 'ended'. If the stage emits 'error' instead of 'ended' and a call later connects, the timer would continue from the old start time.

CallStats.tsx is clean: StyleSheet, testIDs on the card, time, quality, each metric and the pill, tabular-nums, and the timer interval is cleared on unmount. The pill is 32px high (display only, not interactive, so fine).
context_for_next_testing_agent: Two-peer approach: in browser_automation, bt = page.context.browser.browser_type; br = await bt.launch(args=['--use-fake-device-for-media-stream','--use-fake-ui-for-media-stream']); ctx = new_context(viewport 375x667, permissions camera+microphone); open /viewer and /sender; read viewer-code; wait for sender-status 'Camera pronta'; fill sender-code-input; tap sender-call-button. Screenshots must use a .jpg path when quality is given. viewer-recenter-fullscreen-button only renders when motion is on. To reproduce the decline race: after one decline, call again and tap viewer-decline-button with no delay; the sender stays ringing.
rca_of_issue: Decline race: on later calls peerS is already open, so the sender's peerS.connect() (DataConnection) and peerS.call() go out together. The viewer gets the 'call' event and shows Rispondi/Rifiuta before the new DataConnection is open. handlers.decline sends {t:'decline'} only if dc && dc.open; otherwise it silently does nothing and calls attesa.close(). PeerJS does not send a close for an unanswered MediaConnection, so the sender never learns of it and rings until the 45s timeout. On the first call the extra time to open peerS lets the DataConnection open first, which is why the first decline works. Repro: see context_for_next_testing_agent. Mitigation: queue the decline until dc 'open', or have the sender treat a data channel or call close during ringing as a decline.
